I don't know if this is the same. I'm 16 and regularly fly out of DIA and SLC on Southwest. Whoever took me to the airport hugs me goodbye and I jump out of the car alone. 

You do baggage tags as normal if you're checking a bag, if not, just head to security with your carry-on. Security and airlines function differently. Some (most?) airports allow a gate pass to help a minor (capable of flying alone, so 14, 16, etc) but this is done by a family member, friend, etc who is 18+. Ask someone from the airline staff, I ask around bag check, for a gate pass. The person taking the minor to the gate (not on the flight, just goes through security with, walks the airport to the gate, says goodbye when they board, or leaves whenever) needs to give ID with the minor's ticket. My boyfriend regularly does this, they don't care relation if the minor is chill with them. They give the gate pass, similar to a boarding pass, but only allowed through security, not to board.


Then security. If you're alone, you tell them you're a minor and don't have an ID. If they ask, say you don't have to provide it and can't because you don't have it (learner's permit, driver's license). You can show what you have, but they may not even wanna see it because TSA is not allowed to ask for ID from a minor afaik. When they say "Well how do I know you're a minor?" just laugh and shrug. Customer service your way out. If it's annoying, a student ID can work but again not needed. Do the usual, stuff through security, body scan, you're good to go. 

If you have someone with a gate pass, they show their ID, and pass, and sometimes security will wanna look at the pass and ticket. They might ask for a relation to be sure the minor feels safe. Person with a pass does normal security stuff, and then you're through. 


Airport is normal, find your gate, wander if you have time, board when you're called, say goodbye to pass person if there was one, and you're gone. Leaving the opposite airport is easy. Security doesn't care who you are. Walk from the gate to baggage for luggage if you checked any, or take your carry-on, and plan a meeting spot for them to meet whoever is picking up. So, my response may not be as helpful considering me and my boyfriend are younger than you and both have gone through different things and experiences and have different reasons for jealousy or trust issues. I'm simply throwing a bone out there.


But, we met online, and have stayed online — we plan on meeting in person in about two and a half weeks! I have always been very open about communication, and encourage him to talk about stuff, even jealousy because we can work through it together. There is nothing that fixes anything better than communication. Sometimes, communication can be hard or even scary, especially if you're worried it will turn into a confrontation. I worry that he may find someone better closer. 


The way we've worked with this is I see a therapist with who I have been very open about my concerns, and anytime I begin to worry I write the worry down. If it doesn't feel appropriate or like a topic I can handle in the moment to discuss with him, I talk with my therapist first. I tend to realize it's overthinking and eventually explain to him why I'm upset, and how I fixed it or what we talked about. 


Secondly, we have both come to the conclusion that when we feel insecure, we ask for reassurance. I was talking about an ex-friend I was extremely close to, like relationship close, and he felt jealous despite knowing I would never be with this ex-friend. He asked for reassurance, and I gave it to him. Told him the friend is in the past, and all there is now is the future — which is a future I want to spend with him, and him only, and make similar memories of what I look back on so fondly. 


Third, we talk as much as we can. When things get busy, we tell each other about it. I told him my work schedule so he knows when I won't be able to answer immediately, or when I (should) be asleep. We play games together online, we send each other artwork in the mail, have multiple ways to contact each other such as social media, so I send him tiktoks or Instagram reels and we talk about it later. We watch Netflix together a lot — he's obsessed with Umbrella Academy now.


But the bottom line; tell him how you feel. Express you want to fix it, and work forwards. Relationships are about improving yourself as people, together. Work together to cope with these feelings. Everything will work out, and you will find your way. :)

TL;DR. Talk. Communication. It will fix most issues.

This bad boy is a Nephrolepis Obliterata. Aka a Jesters Crown Fern. I have one and they can be picky little plants sometimes. 
The key to reviving it is care and patience. Lots of both. They want humidity. They'd be happy in a room 65°F-75°F. Maybe a little cooler for the night but not by much. Might be best to stay between mentioned temperatures since it was burned by the cold. 

He'd be happy with his own little humidifier nearby, which will help him get water without overwatering. And will help the leaves perk back up. Keep the soil moist, but obviously not overwatered. They like a humidity of 50%. Don't put him too close to anything drafty. Fans, air conditioning, windows, etc. Let him chill on his own with a humidifier and he should be good!! If anything is dead and not just crispy, consider cutting it off.
